title: The globular star cluster NGC 6362
caption: The globular cluster NGC 6362, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 6362 · constellation Ara · about 25000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This colorful view shows NGC 6362, a brilliant ball of ancient stars in the southern constellation Ara, the Altar. It was recorded at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile by the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope.

NGC 6362 is a globular cluster lying about 25,000 light-years away. Globular clusters are dense, roughly spherical collections of stars bound tightly by gravity, and their stars are typically very old, formed early in the history of their galaxy.

Because nearly all their stars formed at about the same time, globular clusters act as fossils, preserving a record of conditions long ago. Differences in color among their stars largely reflect differences in temperature and in how far each star has progressed through its life.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (28.51 x 27.77 arcminutes) and distance (25000 light years), the frame spans roughly 207 × 202 light-years. Its light set out about 25,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and I filters, from visible light into the near-infrared. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The I-band light is near-infrared and invisible to the eye, and the long exposures separate stars the eye could never pick out.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The picture combines exposures through B, V and I filters, spanning visible light into the near-infrared. A wide-field camera like this one can capture the whole cluster and its surroundings in a single view.
alt: A colorful, brilliant ball of ancient stars.
